failure-mode.0: Does not describe what actually fails.
failure-mode.1: Names the failing dependency but not the concrete symptom (exception, timeout, empty result).
failure-mode.2: Describes the concrete failure and where in the request path it surfaces.
failure-mode.3: Describes the failure, the exact error path, and any cascading effect on other components.

detection.0: No indication of how the failure would be noticed.
detection.1: Says 'logs will show it' without naming the log, status code or metric.
detection.2: Names the status code, log line or metric that surfaces the failure.
detection.3: Explains how a developer or monitor distinguishes this failure from similar ones.

recovery.0: No recovery or retry behaviour described.
recovery.1: Mentions retry or crash without saying which one actually happens.
recovery.2: States what the system does next (retry, fail fast, degrade) and where that is implemented.
recovery.3: Explains the recovery strategy, its limits (backoff, max attempts), and what the caller sees meanwhile.

user-impact.0: Does not say what the user experiences.
user-impact.1: Says 'the user gets an error' without the shape of that error.
user-impact.2: Describes the UI state and the message or redirect the user sees.
user-impact.3: Describes the UI state, whether data is lost, and what the user can do to recover.

hints: Name the dependency that fails and the exact symptom.
Follow the error to the status code or log line that proves it.
Say what the user sees on screen, not just what the server logs.
